text: x One following: (1) square, symmetric matrix row names.  (2) vector hyphenated names, identify individual items factor levels "strsplit(..., '-')".  (3) object class "dist". x (x[1]) already class "logical", replaced .call(compare, list(x, threshold)), default converts numbers (typically p-values) less 0.05 TRUE everything else FALSE. x matrix, diagonal must must convert FALSE. compare function binary operator; used class(x) "logical". threshold Second (reference) argument "compare". sep Concatenation character names objects identical similarity / dissimilarity patterns.  output multcompTs matrix number rows = (number columns + number uses "sep" character).

object class "multcompTs", matrix values -1, 0, 1, one row level compared one column "T", read follows: 1 = base "T" represented column, 0 = level(s) significantly different, (-1) = levels(s) significantly different.  two levels pattern significant insignificant differences, combined single column can represented "T" multiple bases.  column name character string concatenating row names "1" column separated "sep" character.  Thus, matrix many 1's rows.  Also, lower triangular portion many "-1's" "TRUE" (e.g., significant) differences among comparisons.

Produces matrix class "multcompTs", describing "undifferentiated classes" identify factor levels items distinct significantly different "base" "T"; two levels pattern significant differences, two combined one "T" two "bases".  resulting T's similar "undifferentiated classes" discussed Donaghue (2004).

John R. Donaghue (2004) "Implementing Shaffer's multiple comparison procedure large number groups", pp. 1-23 Benjamini, Bretz Sarkar (eds) Recent Developments Multiple Comparison Procedures (Institute Mathematical Statistics Lecture Notes-Monograph Series vol. 47) Spencer Graves Hans-Peter Piepho (2006) "Simple Visualizations Paired Comparisons". See  system.file("extdata", "VisualizingPairedComparisons.pdf", package = "multcompView").
